The memory bank's most recent assessment (Step 10 status) has already ruled out the double-destruction theory you were investigating: the nullptr guard at line 175 (`if (g_custom_heap)`) combined with setting `g_custom_heap = nullptr` at line 178 prevents the second shutdown() call from executing the destructor/free logic again.

The memory bank points you back to the original hypothesis: "static libstdc++ objects being destroyed after custom heap cleanup." This aligns with your Step 9 fix strategy: use user_init() (called at line 146, before g_custom_heap is set up at line 149) to initialize stdlib features early, ensuring their static objects use regular malloc rather than the custom heap.

The crash pattern supports this: it happens during shutdown after the custom heap is destroyed, only in release mode (which has a different libstdc++ with different static initialization patterns), and Valgrind doesn't catch it (because Valgrind's instrumentation changes timing and allocation patterns).

You have the fix strategy already identified. Time to implement it in user.cpp.
